about: Giulio Cocchi was a young pastry chef who settled in Asti and in 1891 began making aromatised and sparkling wines. His Vermouth di Torino became one of the classic house styles of the region, and the recipes he wrote down are still the backbone of the range. Since 1978 the company has belonged to the Bava winemaking family, who restored Cocchi’s original formulas; winemaker Giulio Bava oversees production today, in the hills of Cocconato in the Asti province.

Dopo Teatro, “after the theatre,” revives the style Turin’s cafés poured late in the evening for theatregoers. It starts from Cocchi’s Storico Vermouth di Torino, a Moscato-based vermouth made since 1891, to which Bava adds Nebbiolo wine and a measure of Cocchi’s Barolo Chinato for gentle tannin. The wormwood base is reinforced with rhubarb root, quassia wood, gentian, chiretta and a double infusion of cinchona (quina) bark, and it is bottled at 16% alcohol.

The result sits between a vermouth and an amaro: bittersweet, with the structure of Nebbiolo and Barolo Chinato beneath the roots and bark. It is lower in alcohol than a spirit-based amaro, closer to a glass of wine. Tradition says to serve it as the Turin cafés did after the curtain fell, well chilled in a small glass with a twist of lemon zest.
facts: Moscato-based Vermouth di Torino, with Nebbiolo and Barolo Chinato
Wormwood, rhubarb, quassia, gentian, chiretta, cinchona
Well chilled, with a lemon twist
